title: Rabban Gamliel Is Removed from Office
text:
Rabban Gamliel was head of the academy at Yavneh. The Talmud tells that a student once asked Rabbi Yehoshua whether the evening prayer was obligatory, and he said it was optional. The student then asked Rabban Gamliel, who said it was obligatory, and added that Rabbi Yehoshua had told him otherwise.

Rabban Gamliel waited until the scholars were assembled. Then the question was raised in public, and he asked whether anyone disagreed. Rabbi Yehoshua said no. Rabban Gamliel told him that the opposite had been reported in his name, and ordered him to stand up so the witness could testify against him. Rabbi Yehoshua stood. Rabban Gamliel went on teaching and left him standing, until the assembly began to murmur and told the speaker to stop. It was not the first time Rabban Gamliel had humiliated Rabbi Yehoshua this way, they said, and they removed him from office. In his place they appointed the young Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah. That day the guard at the door was removed, and so many new students came that hundreds of benches had to be added.

Rabban Gamliel went to Rabbi Yehoshua's house to apologize. Seeing its blackened walls, he learned that Rabbi Yehoshua earned his living as a smith or charcoal maker. Rabbi Yehoshua told him that a generation led by someone who did not know how scholars struggled to live was to be pitied. Rabban Gamliel asked his forgiveness, and received it. In the end, the sages arranged for him to share the leadership with Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah.
lesson: Winning an argument by humiliating a colleague can cost you the trust that holds your position up. When you have done harm, go yourself, admit it and ask to be forgiven.
people: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah
